title: Specimen
deck: Typeset reading editions of PureScript libraries, generated from the code itself. The banner over each book is its dependency graph — every plate a module, its declarations packed by size, import order running left to right. The timelines share one scale.

shelves.title: Core Libraries
shelves.blurb: The standard library in the broad sense: the packages nearly every PureScript program stands on. They change rarely, and on purpose — read them to learn how the language wants to be written.

shelves.title: Further Reading
shelves.blurb: Beautiful constructions worth reading for their own sake: the free monad and its relatives, and the classic parser-combinator library.

shelves.title: The Rowtype-Yoga Project
shelves.blurb: Pragmatic packages built on PureScript's row types, from the rowtype-yoga organisation — JSON without boilerplate, and friends.

shelves.title: Surgical Instruments
shelves.blurb: Very sharp tools for very specific cuts. Code this dense is a standing temptation to keep writing JavaScript, just with an extraordinary amount of type noise — but where a polymorphic variant or a heterogeneous fold is genuinely needed, nothing else will do. Presented here as instruments: read slowly, use sparingly.

prelude.text: Begin here. End here, years later.

foldable-traversable.text: The whole doctrine of iteration in eleven modules.

transformers.text: A tower you can actually climb.

tailrec.text: One module. No stack. All heart.

free.text: Structure for nothing, interpretation for all.

parsing.text: Reads everything, so you don't have to.

footnote: Release timelines show the PureScript registry's record, which begins with the registry itself (2017–18); several of these libraries are older, and legacy re-imports can carry recent timestamps. The quiet stretches are the point — in this ecosystem a library that hasn't changed in years is usually finished, not abandoned.
